sources.title: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology §14.1 — sensory perception, covering the ear, the cochlea and hair cell transduction

visual.title: Impedance, tonotopy and the hair cell
visual.alt: The outer, middle and inner ear in sequence with the impedance-matching arithmetic of the middle ear; the basilar membrane drawn unrolled as a wedge, narrow and stiff at the base and wide at the apex, labelled from twenty kilohertz at the oval window down to twenty hertz at the helicotrema; a five-step account of hair cell transduction from stereocilia shear through tip links and potassium entry to glutamate release; and a contrast of conductive against sensorineural hearing loss.
visual.caption: The membrane is a ruler for frequency. Which part of it moves decides the pitch you hear, and that same map is carried all the way to cortex.
visual.beforeHeading: ### The Basilar Membrane and Frequency Tuning
